evals.prompt: As a principal software architect, do a review and audit of the existing codebase. DO NOT modify code. Just write out a plan if you detect any issues.
evals.expected_output: The audit skill runs read-only across the whole repo, fans out to parallel personas, and produces a single plan file under docs/plans/. No source file is edited, no branch is created, nothing is staged or committed.
expectations: Uses no Edit tool call on any file
Uses no Write tool call except for the single plan file under docs/plans/
Runs no state-changing git command (no checkout -b, add, commit, stash, restore, push)
Defaults the scope to the whole repo without asking the user to narrow it
Launches multiple persona subagents in a single message so they run concurrently
Persona set covers principal engineer, security engineer, test engineer and technical writer lenses
Every reported finding cites a concrete file path and line number
Writes exactly one plan file at docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.md
Plan contains a scope section, a severity-ranked findings table, per-finding detail, and a remediation order
Does not stage or commit the plan file
Chat reply gives the plan path and a severity count rather than pasting the whole plan

evals.prompt: Audit and assess whether all the providers in packages/auth are implemented properly and properly dependency injected, with no bleeding across providers. Ignore the specs in the @docs folder, they may not be valid anymore.
evals.expected_output: The audit is scoped to packages/auth plus its direct dependents, the docs/ directory is excluded from every persona prompt and the exclusion is recorded in the plan scope, and findings about DI and provider boundaries are grounded in real file:line citations.
expectations: Scopes the audit to packages/auth and its direct dependents rather than the whole repo
Excludes the docs/ directory from the audit and passes that exclusion to every persona
Records the docs/ exclusion in the plan's scope section
Edits no code and creates no branch
The principal engineer lens explicitly examines dependency injection, singletons or globals, and cross-provider imports
Verifies each claimed cross-provider import by reading the cited import line before reporting it
Does not report a symbol or module that does not exist in the codebase
Writes the plan to docs/plans/ with stable A-prefixed finding ids
Sizes each remediation item so it fits one subagent task

evals.prompt: Please take a look at @docs/plans/2026-09-02-1130-token-rotation-plan.md and see if it has merits. Critique the approach, see if the concerns are valid. Any changes or issues we should address?
evals.expected_output: The skill enters plan critique mode: it reads the plan, checks every claim it makes about the codebase against the actual code, classifies each stated concern as valid, already mitigated, or not a real problem with evidence, names hidden risks, and writes a critique file without touching the plan being critiqued or any code.
expectations: Reads the referenced plan document in full before commenting
Does not edit the plan document being critiqued
Does not edit any source file and creates no branch
Verifies each claim the plan makes about the codebase against real files, citing file:line
Produces a verdict per stated concern: valid, already mitigated, or not a real problem
Flags any concern that is already handled in the code, citing the line that handles it
Names hidden risks the plan does not mention, such as migration, backwards compatibility, error paths or half-finished state
Writes the critique to a new docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>-critique.md file
Ends with lettered options and a stated recommendation

evals.prompt: Do an assessment of the repo to make sure there are no code smells or risks. Write a plan file with the identified issues and suggested fixes. DO NOT EDIT ANY CODE AT THIS TIME.
evals.expected_output: A whole-repo audit producing a correctly located and correctly structured plan file whose findings carry stable ids that execute-plan can reference later.
expectations: Runs `date` or an equivalent to get the real timestamp for the filename rather than guessing a date
Writes the plan at docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.md with a kebab-case slug naming the target
Creates no other file and edits no existing file
Every finding has a stable id of the form A1, A2, A3
Ids in the findings table match the ids used in the per-finding detail sections and in the remediation order
Findings table has columns for id, severity, file:line location, finding, and suggested fix
Severity values are limited to Critical, High, Medium and Low
Each suggested fix names a verification command taken from the repo's package.json scripts rather than an invented one
Remediation order lists items sized as individual subagent tasks
Plan file is not staged or committed
